questions.question: What are the two types of endpoints required for proper Braze SDK integration?
questions.explanation: For proper integration, you need the REST endpoint for API calls and the SDK endpoint for client-side SDK implementations. Using the REST endpoint for SDK integration is incorrect and will cause errors.

questions.question: How is authentication handled in Braze REST API requests?
options: Using username and password in the request body
Using the REST API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header
questions.explanation: Braze authenticates REST API requests using the REST API key passed as a Bearer token in the Authorization header: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_REST_API_KEY.

questions.question: What is the default rate limit for Braze REST API endpoints?
questions.explanation: The default rate limit for most Braze REST API endpoints is 250,000 requests per hour per workspace, though some request types have their own limits.

questions.question: True or False: You should use the REST endpoint for SDK initialization in mobile apps.
questions.explanation: False. You must use the SDK endpoint for SDK initialization, not the REST endpoint. Using the wrong endpoint will result in initialization failures.

questions.question: What is the importance of the external_id in Braze integration?
options: It's only used for analytics reporting
It serves as a unique user identifier and must match the user ID set in the SDK to avoid creating duplicate profiles
It's only required for API requests
It's used only for email campaigns
questions.explanation: The external_id is a critical identifier that must be consistent across the SDK and API. Using different IDs for the same user will create multiple profiles.

questions.question: Which of the following are REST API best practices in Braze? (Select 2)
options: Only send delta values (changed data) to improve efficiency
Send all user data on every request for consistency
Implement error handling and retry logic
questions.explanation: Best practices include batching requests to improve performance and implementing proper error handling. Sending only changed data (delta values) is more efficient than sending all data every time.

questions.question: What is a webhook in the context of Braze integration?
options: A tool for designing email templates
An HTTP callback that sends data from Braze to external systems in real-time based on user actions
questions.explanation: Webhooks are HTTP callbacks that allow Braze to send data to your external systems in real-time when specific events occur, enabling event-driven integrations.

questions.question: True or False: Braze webhooks can only be triggered by user actions.
questions.explanation: False. Webhooks can be triggered by various events including user actions, campaign events, or API calls. They're flexible and event-driven.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Braze SDK in an application?
options: To store user data on the device
To track user behavior, collect data, and deliver messaging channels (push, in-app, Content Cards)
To replace the REST API entirely
questions.explanation: The Braze SDK serves two main functions: collecting and syncing user data, and powering messaging channels like push notifications and in-app messages.

questions.question: When should you use the Braze REST API instead of the SDK?
options: For backend operations like sending transactional messages, bulk user imports, and data that isn't generated from user devices
questions.explanation: The REST API is ideal for server-side operations, bulk updates, and data flows that don't come from user devices, like systems updating customer status.

questions.question: What is a test environment in Braze development?
options: The production environment with restricted features
A separate workspace with its own API key used for development and QA to prevent test data from polluting production
A feature that's only available in mobile SDKs
questions.explanation: A test environment is a separate Braze workspace with its own API key, used during development and QA to prevent test data from contaminating production data.

questions.question: What does IP allowlisting (whitelisting) provide in Braze REST API?
options: A security feature that restricts REST API requests to specified IP addresses or subnets
questions.explanation: IP allowlisting is a security feature that restricts which IP addresses can make REST API requests using a given API key, providing an additional security layer.

questions.question: Which content type should you expect in Braze webhook payloads?
questions.explanation: Braze sends webhook data in JSON format, which allows you to parse structured data containing event information and user attributes.

questions.question: True or False: Braze will overwrite all attributes even if you only intended to update one.
questions.explanation: True. Braze overwrites every attribute that is sent in an API request. Therefore, you should only send attributes that have actually changed (delta values) to avoid unintended overwriting.

questions.question: What is the typical integration timeline for Braze according to best practices?
options: 1-6 weeks depending on technical skills and breadth
questions.explanation: Braze typically takes 1-6 weeks to integrate, depending on your team's technical skills, bandwidth, and the complexity of your implementation.

questions.question: Which REST API permissions are commonly required for user data management?
options: users.track for sending data and users.export.ids for retrieving user data
questions.explanation: Different API operations require different permissions. users.track is needed to send/update user data, while users.export.ids is needed to export user information.

questions.question: When integrating Braze with multiple root domains, what should you consider?
options: Using a single app with one API key vs. separate apps for each domain
Always create separate apps for each domain
Always use a single app regardless of domain
questions.explanation: For Web SDK implementations spanning multiple root domains, Braze recommends evaluating whether to use one app or separate apps to avoid session tracking issues.

questions.question: How should you handle webhook failures in a production system?
options: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and logging for debugging
questions.explanation: Production webhook handling should include retry mechanisms with exponential backoff, error logging, and monitoring to ensure data consistency.

questions.question: What happens if you send an API request with a user ID that doesn't exist in Braze?
options: The request fails with an error
A new user profile is created with that ID
questions.explanation: Braze will create a new user profile with that external_id if it doesn't already exist, preventing you from creating unintended duplicate profiles.

questions.question: True or False: The REST API can be used to trigger campaigns and Canvas directly.
questions.explanation: True. The Braze REST API allows you to trigger campaigns and Canvas through API endpoints, enabling event-driven messaging workflows.

questions.question: What should be the first step when setting up a Braze SDK in a mobile application?
options: Initializing the SDK with the API key and SDK endpoint
questions.explanation: SDK initialization with the correct API key and SDK endpoint must be done first, as all other SDK functionality depends on successful initialization.

questions.question: Which of the following data ingestion methods are supported by Braze? (Select 2)
options: Batch CSV uploads for one-time data import
questions.explanation: Braze supports multiple data ingestion methods: REST API for real-time backend updates, SDK for client-side tracking, and CSV uploads for batch imports. Email is a channel, not an ingestion method.

questions.question: What security consideration is important when receiving Braze webhooks?
options: Verify the webhook signature and HTTPS to ensure authenticity and integrity
Security is only for REST API
questions.explanation: You should verify webhook signatures and ensure HTTPS is used to validate that webhooks actually come from Braze and haven't been tampered with.

questions.question: What is the role of sessionization in Braze SDK?
options: It groups user interactions into sessions by generating open and close session events
questions.explanation: The Braze SDK automatically generates 'open session' and 'close session' events to group user interactions into sessions, enabling session-based analytics and retention.

questions.question: What is the benefit of batching REST API requests?
options: It reduces the number of API calls, improves performance, and can be more cost-effective
questions.explanation: Batching requests reduces the number of API calls, improves throughput, decreases latency, and is a Braze best practice for efficient API usage.

questions.question: How should you handle the changeUser() method in multi-device scenarios?
options: Call it once at app startup
Call it every time a user logs in to ensure each device is associated with the correct user ID
questions.explanation: In multi-device scenarios, you should call changeUser() when a user logs in to ensure their device is correctly associated with their user profile and avoid data mixing.

questions.question: True or False: Custom attributes in Braze are case-insensitive.
questions.explanation: False. Custom attributes are case-sensitive. 'user_tier' and 'User_Tier' would be treated as different attributes.

questions.question: What types of user events can trigger Braze webhooks?
options: Campaign clicks and app opens only
Custom events, purchase events, session events, and campaign interactions
questions.explanation: Braze webhooks can be triggered by various user events including custom events, purchases, sessions, clicks, and other engagement interactions.

questions.question: When making changes to your Braze REST API key, what should you do if it's been accidentally exposed?
options: Nothing, it's not a security concern
Delete the exposed key from the Developer Console immediately to prevent unauthorized access
Wait and monitor for suspicious activity
Create a new API key without deleting the old one
questions.explanation: If a REST API key is accidentally exposed, you should delete it immediately from the Developer Console to prevent unauthorized access to your Braze instance.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for testing Braze integration before going to production?
options: Use a separate test workspace with its own API key, test all functionality, and verify data doesn't reach production
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use a dedicated test/staging environment with its own Braze workspace and API key to thoroughly test before deploying to production.
